code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.h(1)
qc.cx(1, 0)
claim: This prepares the Bell state (|00> + |11>)/√2 by applying Hadamard to q[1] and CNOT with q[1] as control and q[0] as target.

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.x(0)
claim: This prepares |01> by applying X to q[0], flipping it from |0> to |1>.

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(1)
qc.h(0)
qc.z(0)
claim: This prepares |-> = (|0> - |1>)/√2 by applying Hadamard followed by Z gate to q[0].

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(1)
qc.rz(3.141592653589793, 0)
claim: This implements the Pauli Z gate using RZ(π), which produces the same effect up to a global phase.

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(1)
qc.ry(1.0471975511965976, 0)
claim: This applies the RY gate with angle π/3 to q[0].

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.cx(1, 0)
claim: This applies CNOT with q[1] as control and q[0] as target.

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(3)
qc.h(0)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.cx(0, 2)
claim: This prepares the 3-qubit GHZ state (|000> + |111>)/√2 using Hadamard on q[0] followed by CNOTs to q[1] and q[2].

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.cp(1.5707963267948966, 0, 1)
claim: This applies the controlled-phase gate CP(π/2) with q[0] as control and q[1] as target, producing the diagonal matrix diag(1, 1, 1, i).

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.h(1)
qc.cp(1.5707963267948966, 0, 1)
qc.h(0)
qc.swap(0, 1)
claim: This implements the 2-qubit QFT including final qubit reversal by applying Hadamard and controlled-phase gates in the correct order then swapping qubits.

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.swap(0, 1)
qc.h(0)
qc.cp(-1.5707963267948966, 0, 1)
qc.h(1)
claim: This implements the inverse of the 2-qubit QFT by applying gates in reverse order with negated controlled-phase angle.

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(3)
qc.ccx(0, 1, 2)
claim: This applies the Toffoli gate with q[0] and q[1] as controls and q[2] as target.

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(2, 2)
qc.h(1)
qc.cx(1, 0)
qc.measure([0, 1], [0, 1])
claim: This prepares the Bell state (|00> + |11>)/√2 and measures both q[0] and q[1] into classical bits c[0] and c[1].

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.h(0)
qc.x(1)
claim: This prepares |+> on q[0] using Hadamard and |1> on q[1] using X gate, with no measurements.

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.cx(1, 0)
qc.cx(0, 1)
claim: This swaps the states of q[0] and q[1] using three CNOT gates in the standard decomposition.

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(4)
qc.mct([0, 1, 2], 3)
claim: This applies X to q[3] controlled on q[0], q[1], and q[2] all being 1, using the multi-controlled Toffoli gate.
